texts.preamble: The State Of West Bengal & Ors vs Sami Saikh on 5 February, 2026 Ct. No.4 D/L 05.02.2026 (Naba) 10 W.P.S.T. 128 of 2023 The State of West Bengal & Ors. Vs. Sami Saikh Mr. Tapan Kumar Mukherjee, ld. A.G.P., Ms. Saheli Mukherjee ...for the State Responden
texts.facts: It was the writ petitioner's contention before the West Bengal Administrative Tribunal ('Tribunal' for short) that the experience (five years) was required only for those who held no degree; but were holding the equivalent qualification. The petitioner challenged the order in W.P.S.T. No. 103 of 2023. The application is allowed. Hence the West Bengal Health Recruitment Board and its Chairman, the respondent Nos.3 and 4 respectively, are directed to consider the candidature of the applicant on merit for the post of Deputy Food Supply Inspecting Officer within four weeks from the date of presentation of a copy of the certified copy of the order." 5. The writ The State Of West Bengal & Ors vs Sami Saikh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31267170/ 1 petitioner was found not to be possessing any Doctorate degree and, therefore, no marks could be granted in respect thereof. The writ petitioner was also found not to be possessing essential five years experience in State/Government contract. The total mark awarded was 35. Moreover, in the interview, he was found not to be able to answer the questions put to him. The writ petitioner participated in the selection process to the post of District Food Safety and Inspecting Officer. His candidature was considered once prior to the intervention of the Court. His candidature was assessed afresh after order of Court. In both the opportunities, the was not successful. In fact, he was found not to be possessing some of the essential qualifications required.
